observations.epoch_band_state_and_other_notes: Exact SIMBAD alias chain and Gaia DR3 ID confirm the optical counterpart. Short-period CV with DN-like optical spectrum but novalike-survey membership; subtype/state unresolved. Radio is an upper limit only (<24 uJy, MeerKAT; Hewitt+20). 1.5093 h is the most probable photometric alias, not a secure orbital period; P4=0.060972(14) d remains viable. Ridder+23 X-ray fluxes are model conversions with unspecified source-specific absorption convention; 2RXS is a low-count detection with centroid about 19.2 arcsec from Gaia propagated to J2000 and requires localization review.

issues.competing_evidence: Tappert+04 Table 7: P3=0.062887(37)d (pd=.637 most probable) and P4=0.060972(14)d (pd=.272 important); five aliases total and more observations needed. Hewitt+20 repeats P3 as Porb.
issues.why_it_matters: A canonical orbit affects period distributions, donor sequence and evolutionary comparisons.
issues.needed_action: Keep P3 as a candidate only; use follow-up photometry/spectroscopy to confirm before promoting to secure orbital period.

issues.competing_evidence: Tappert calls spectrum DN-like with strong H-alpha; Hewitt includes source in novalike sample but allows missed-outburst DN.
issues.needed_action: Retain provisional DN-like CV/novalike-sample membership with subtype unresolved unless light-curve/outburst evidence warrants a final label.

issues.competing_evidence: 2RXS row links to 1RXS at 0.7 arcsec, SIMBAD links 1RXS to V5662/Gaia, but 2RXS centroid is ~19.2 arcsec from Gaia propagated J2000 and has only 18.71+/-5.11 counts.
issues.why_it_matters: The counterpart decides whether ROSAT properties belong to this CV.
issues.needed_action: Inspect 2RXS images/localization or ROSAT event products and decide whether to accept the catalog link; keep flux qualified pending review.

references.note: MeerKAT study of 11 novalike CVs; local PDF text audited for CM Phe table values Porb=0.2689(7) d, distance 315.1 +/-3.8 pc, radio non-detection <30 microJy at 0.43-2.1 GHz, radio luminosity upper limit 4.6e15 erg/s/Hz, Hoard+01 M2-5 donor citation, identity-confusion note, and disk SED assumptions Mwd=0.75 Msun, M2=0.5 Msun, i=57 deg, Mdot=0.7e-9 Msun/yr. Audited for IM Eri: Table 1 gives distance 191.2 +/-1.4 pc and Porb=0.1456348(4) d from Armstrong+13_IMEri; Section 2.5 identifies IM Eri as a non-eclipsing novalike with blue-shifted He I 5876 and super/suborbital signals; Table 3 gives first radio detection 99 +/-26 microJy, Lnu=4.3 +/-1.1e15 erg/s/Hz, alpha=1.2 +/-1.6; Table 4 uses assumed M1=0.75 Msun, M2=0.24 Msun, i=57 deg, Mdot=2.5e-9 Msun/yr for a disk SED model and notes the IM Eri Mdot is particularly uncertain because no UV data and assumed binary parameters. Audited for V347 Pup: Table 1 gives distance 295.8 +/-1.4 pc and Porb=0.231936060(6) d from Thoroughgood+05_V347Pup; Section 2.9 summarizes eclipsing novalike/SW Sex-like nature, possible historical IP suggestion but no coherent optical pulsations/no strong magnetic evidence, q=0.83 +/-0.05, M1=0.63 +/-0.04 Msun, M2=0.52 +/-0.06 Msun, i=84.0 +/-2.3 deg, and M0.5V donor; Table 3 gives radio non-detection <30 microJy; Section 4.1 notes a weak 28 +/-14 microJy signal was rejected as below 5sigma/offset/not beam-consistent; Table 4 uses Mdot=6e-9 Msun/yr. Audited for IX Vel: Table 1 gives distance 90.6 +/-0.2 pc and Porb=0.193929(2) d from BeuermannThomas+90_IXVel; Section 2.1 describes IX Vel as brightest night-sky CV, gives M1=0.80 +0.16/-0.11 Msun and M2=0.52 +0.10/-0.07 Msun from Beuermann & Thomas, Mdot=5e-9 Msun/yr and i=57 +/-2 deg from Linnell+07_IXVel, and P-Cygni UV wind outflows ~3000 km/s; Table 3 gives MeerKAT non-detection <42 microJy and Lnu<0.4e15 erg/s/Hz; Section 4.4 gives SED-preferred Mdot~7e-9 Msun/yr. Audited for RW Sex: Table 1 gives distance 236.5 +/-5.0 pc and Porb=0.24507(20) d from Beuermann+92_RWSex; Section 2.7 summarizes non-eclipsing novalike, q=0.74 +/-0.10, i=28-40 deg, Linnell+10_RWSex Mdot~5e-9 Msun/yr, K5 donor spectrum from VandePutte+03_RWSex, and disk wind ~4550 km/s; Table 3 gives MeerKAT 0.43-2.1 GHz integrated radio flux 82 +/-23 uJy, Lnu=5.5 +/-1.6e15 erg/s/Hz, alpha=-1.5 +/-1.0; Table 4 SED-model parameters use M1=0.84 Msun, M2=0.62 Msun, i=34 deg, and Mdot=8e-9 Msun/yr, while text notes Linnell+10 optimum Mdot=5.75e-9 Msun/yr at old Hipparcos distance and that Gaia lowered the distance. Audited for LS IV -08 3: Table 1 gives distance 211.0 +/-2.8 pc and Porb=0.1952894(10) d from Stark+08_LSIV-08-3; Section 2.6 describes it as an optically bright novalike with no previous radio observations; Table 3 gives MeerKAT 0.43-2.1 GHz nondetection <33 microJy and Lnu<1.8e15 erg/s/Hz; Table 4 uses assumed/default SED parameters M1=0.75 Msun, M2=0.45 Msun, i=57 deg, and Mdot=5e-9 Msun/yr. Audited for V341 Ara: Table 1 gives distance 156.1 +/-2.0 pc and Porb=0.15216(2) d from BondMiszalski+18_V341Ara; Section 2.3 summarizes novalike classification plus Fr 2-11 and bow-shock nebula context; Table 3 gives MeerKAT 0.43-2.1 GHz nondetection <27 microJy and Lnu<0.8e15 erg/s/Hz; Table 4 uses assumed/default SED parameters M1=0.75 Msun, M2=0.27 Msun, i=30 deg, and Mdot=3.5e-9 Msun/yr. Audited for V3885 Sgr: Table 1 gives distance 132.7 +/-1.4 pc and Porb=0.20716071(22) d from RibeiroDiaz+07_V3885Sgr; Section 2.2 summarizes Hartley+05_V3885Sgr q/mass/inclination constraints and Linnell+09_V3885Sgr Mdot=5 +/-2e-9 Msun/yr; Table 3 gives MeerKAT 0.43-2.1 GHz detection 256 +/-25 uJy, Lnu=5.4 +/-0.5e15 erg/s/Hz, alpha=-0.6 +/-0.7; Table 4 uses SED inputs M1=0.675, M2=0.473, i=60 deg, and Mdot=8e-9 Msun/yr; text summarizes earlier ATCA detections from Koerding+11_V3885Sgr. references.note:
Original arXiv/publisher metadata and article text web-verified: Tappert, Augusteijn & Maza (2004), MNRAS 354, 321-331. For CTCV J2005-2934 (V5662 Sgr), the paper identifies a typical dwarf-nova spectrum with unusually strong Halpha, gives P3=0.062887(37) d as the most probable photometric alias, and explicitly retains P4=0.060972(14) d as an important alias requiring more observations.

Full article checked: Table 3 reports H-alpha EW 219 Å and H-beta EW 66 Å, no He II 4686 detection; Table 7 gives five period-search aliases. P3=0.062887(37) d is the most probable alias (discriminatory power 0.637), while P4=0.060972(14) d remains important (0.272); more observations are needed to identify the orbital period securely.
references.full_citation: Tappert, S., Augusteijn, T., & Maza, J. 2004, Cataclysmic variables from the Calán–Tololo Survey – I. Photometric periods, Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, 354, 321–331.

cmd.distance_uncertainty_convention: Posterior p16/p50/p84; asymmetric, not Gaussian 1-sigma bounds
cmd.adoption_reason: Release-selected distance used; no compatibility absolute magnitude consumed.
cmd.uncertainty_method: Recorded distance endpoints transformed nonlinearly at fixed G; retain the recorded interval convention, including unspecified conventions. Posterior quantiles are not Gaussian errors. Photometric error separate. Color error, where both available, approximates independent BP/RP errors in quadrature; covariance and variability ignored.

cmd.qualifications: Bayesian geometric prior; unresolved system photometry and variability
